message:
Safety-Control Integrator:

Latched trip covers both shutdown causes for Power-Systems Engineer and the Manager. Plain words: a Normally Closed (NC), meaning wired shut until pressed, Emergency Stop (ESTOP), meaning red stop switch, loop in series with a load-voltage tap drives a latching relay, so opening the switch on command or losing load volts trips and stays tripped. I read the CWC 2019 Rules and Requirements Manual_20190104 (E41) which states turbines must be capable of shutting down on command as well as when electrically disconnected from the load and defines shutdown as dropping below 10 percent of maximum Revolutions Per Minute (RPM), meaning shaft turns per minute, within 10 s, and I apply that rule in the latched trip (C20) with trip threshold 315 RPM from 10 percent of the top speed (E13) 3.15e+03 RPM, in the side-view shutdown layout (E50).

Combined friction plus electrical brake stops in time where electrical alone cannot, for Aero-Rotor Lead and Power-Systems Engineer. Plain words: a spring pushes a small disc pad shut on the slow shaft while the generator dumps to a resistor, so spin turns to heat in seconds and the spring holds it parked. I read the Braking ideas for wind turbines (E42) which states almost all wind turbine rotor brakes are of the fail-to-safe design, being spring-applied and released, with powerful springs pressing liners against a disc, and I transfer that rule to the spring disc (C21); the combined stop simulation (E47) with inertia 0.00200 kg·m2 and friction 0.400 N·m crosses below 10 percent in 1.65 s and sits at 0.00 RPM at 10 s, with top Kinetic Energy (KE), meaning spin energy, 109 J and peak friction heat 132 W, while the electrical-only runaway check (E48) reaches 9.12e+03 RPM at 10 s against the 315 RPM limit because 0.155 N·m electrical torque cannot beat 0.480 N·m wind torque, so the dump resistor (C16) alone fails.

Mounting fits Structures-Survival Engineer without changing topology. Plain words: the disc sits on the slow shaft inside the nacelle on bedplate rails, wires run inside the post bore, and the parked hold needs soft stall to keep 22 m/s aero torque below the 0.400 N·m pad. The side-view shutdown layout (E50) shows rotor to hub to shaft to generator plus brake in the nacelle to controller to load, and nacelle to pivot to post below, with only the post outside the cube.

Not ready, because Manager selection between dump-only and spring-plus-dump plus a bench test for re-latch restart still needs decision.
